_note: Goals for /audit. The first argument picks one (default: full). merge.js init copies the chosen goal into run.json, and every agent reads it from there. To add a goal, copy an entry and change it.

full.name: Full audit
full.brief: Review every file for all four categories.

security.name: Security audit
security.brief: Find every way someone could read or change data, use staff powers, take the menu down, or get a secret they shouldn't. Think like an attacker, not a code reviewer: a logged-out visitor, a signed-in customer using the Firebase SDK straight from the browser console, a second customer, a demoted staff member, someone with a stolen staff password, a malicious catalog edit, a fork or pull request against the public repo. Report only security findings. If you trip over a serious non-security bug, report it once with its real category; the report lists it separately and it is not verified.
checklist: database.rules.json: for every path in map.json db_paths, who can read and who can write - logged-out visitor, signed-in customer, another customer, staff, demoted staff. Is the root default-deny? Can anyone add themselves to /staff?
Values the server trusts from the client: dates, stamps, scores, prices, ranks, anything a rule only format-checks
Cloud functions (cloud/): auth required, rank read from the database or from a stale token claim, input validation, what a malicious caller can send, what errors reveal
Injection: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, href and src built from catalog data, database data, URL parameters (location.search, hash) or localStorage

Secrets: keys, tokens or service-account JSON in tracked files or in git history (read-only: git log -p -S<pattern>, git grep). Probe-script dumps covered by .gitignore. Workflows that could print a secret
GitHub Actions: permissions block, actions pinned to a version, secrets reachable from pull_request runs, what GH_DISPATCH_TOKEN can do
Third-party scripts: CDN scripts without integrity attributes, versions, what analytics receives
Customer privacy: does privacy.html match what the code stores and sends; does delete-my-account remove the user node, toastOrders and the Auth record; what export includes
Staff sign-in (employee.html, Merroir): session length, sign-out, what a signed-in non-staff user can see or call
Phone sign-in abuse: SMS cost abuse, App Check or reCAPTCHA, rate limits
